concepts.name: Constitutional Basis and Nature of Impeachment
key_dimensions: Article 61 as the sole constitutional provision governing impeachment
Quasi-judicial nature of the impeachment process vs. purely political process in other democracies
Distinction between impeachment (violation of Constitution) and removal of other constitutional functionaries
Why impeachment is the ONLY way to remove the President — no motion of no-confidence applies

concepts.name: Grounds for Impeachment: 'Violation of the Constitution'
key_dimensions: The term 'violation of the Constitution' is undefined — deliberate constitutional ambiguity
Whether violation includes acts of omission vs. commission
Comparison with US impeachment grounds: 'high crimes and misdemeanors' vs. India's broader/narrower scope debate
UPSC trap: No other ground (e.g., incapacity, misconduct) is valid for impeachment under Article 61

concepts.name: Initiating House: Either House Can Initiate
key_dimensions: Unlike most removal processes, impeachment can be initiated in either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
Contrast with the process for removal of Vice President (only Rajya Sabha initiates)
Contrast with removal of Speaker (only Lok Sabha)
UPSC trap: No special designation of the 'initiating house' — symmetry is a unique feature

concepts.name: Notice Requirement: 14-Day Advance Written Notice
key_dimensions: Minimum 14 days' written notice signed by not less than one-fourth of total membership of the house
Notice must be addressed to the President before the resolution is moved
Purpose: Gives the President opportunity to present a defence
UPSC trap: The one-fourth threshold is for notice; the passing threshold (two-thirds) is different — confusion point

concepts.name: Special Majority Requirement: Two-Thirds of Total Membership
key_dimensions: Resolution must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the TOTAL membership of the house (not just members present and voting)
Critical distinction: 'total membership' vs. 'members present and voting' — a classic UPSC trap
Both houses must separately pass the resolution by two-thirds of total membership
Comparison with Special Majority under Article 368 (two-thirds present and voting + majority of total) — different standard

concepts.name: Role of the Investigating House
key_dimensions: After the initiating house passes the resolution, it is sent to the other house for investigation
The other house sits as an investigating body — quasi-judicial function
The President has the right to appear and be represented during investigation
The investigating house must also pass the resolution by two-thirds of total membership for impeachment to succeed

concepts.name: President's Right to Defence During Impeachment
key_dimensions: Article 61(3): President has the right to appear and be represented at such investigation
Can be represented by a counsel — legal representation is constitutionally guaranteed
Principle of audi alteram partem embedded in the impeachment process
UPSC angle: This makes it quasi-judicial — compare with removal of Supreme Court judge under Article 124 where judge also has representation rights

concepts.name: Participation of Both Houses: No Joint Sitting
key_dimensions: Both houses act separately and sequentially — no provision for a joint sitting in impeachment
Contrast with ordinary legislative deadlock resolved by joint sitting under Article 108
UPSC trap: Joint sitting is NOT applicable to Constitutional Amendment Bills or Money Bills — same principle of exclusion applies to impeachment
Sequential process: House 1 passes → House 2 investigates and passes → President removed

concepts.name: Elected vs. Nominated Members' Voting Rights in Impeachment
key_dimensions: Both elected AND nominated members of Parliament participate in impeachment — unlike Presidential election
Presidential election excludes nominated members; impeachment INCLUDES them
State Legislative Assembly members have NO role in impeachment (unlike Presidential election)
UPSC high-yield trap: Nominated MPs vote in impeachment but NOT in Presidential/VP election

concepts.name: Role of State Legislatures in Impeachment
key_dimensions: State Legislative Assemblies have ZERO role in the impeachment process
Contrast with Presidential election where elected members of State Assemblies participate
Federalism angle: Impeachment is purely a parliamentary (central) function
UPSC trap: Students often confuse election (federal) with removal (purely parliamentary)

concepts.name: Effect of Dissolution of Lok Sabha on Impeachment Proceedings
key_dimensions: No explicit constitutional provision addresses what happens if Lok Sabha is dissolved mid-impeachment
Scholarly debate: Whether proceedings lapse or continue in reconstituted Lok Sabha
Contrast with Article 108 (joint sitting) which has specific lapsing provisions
Practical significance: Has never been tested — theoretical UPSC question zone

concepts.name: Comparison with Removal of Vice President
key_dimensions: Vice President removed by Rajya Sabha resolution + Lok Sabha concurrence (Article 67b) — asymmetric
President's impeachment: Either house can initiate — symmetric
VP removal: Simple majority of all members of Rajya Sabha; President: Two-thirds of total membership
UPSC trap: Different majority thresholds and different initiating house rules for President vs. VP

concepts.name: Comparison with Removal of Supreme Court Judges
key_dimensions: Article 124(4): SC judge removed by Presidential order after address by each House passed by special majority
SC judge removal: Initiated by Parliament, executed by President — reverse of impeachment
Both require two-thirds majority but the procedural actor roles are inverted
Judges Inquiry Act 1968 adds procedural layer for SC judges — no equivalent statute for Presidential impeachment

concepts.name: No Impeachment of Vice President Under Article 61
key_dimensions: Article 61 applies ONLY to the President — VP has a separate, simpler removal mechanism
UPSC trap: Confusing the impeachment procedure (Article 61) with VP removal (Article 67)
The word 'impeachment' does not appear in Article 67 — removal of VP is NOT called impeachment constitutionally
Only the President can be 'impeached' in Indian constitutional terminology

concepts.name: Historical Record: No Impeachment Has Ever Occurred in India
key_dimensions: No President of India has ever been successfully impeached
Motion against V.V. Giri was contemplated but never formally initiated
Political significance: The high threshold (two-thirds of total membership of both houses) makes impeachment practically very difficult
Contrast with US where impeachments have occurred — India's design is more conservative

concepts.name: Interaction Between Impeachment and Presidential Immunity (Article 361)
key_dimensions: Article 361: President not answerable to any court for exercise of powers and duties
Impeachment is the ONLY accountability mechanism — courts cannot intervene during tenure
Whether a President can be criminally prosecuted after impeachment is a grey area
UPSC angle: Article 361 immunity and Article 61 impeachment together define the accountability architecture

concepts.name: Effectiveness Date of Removal Upon Successful Impeachment
key_dimensions: President stands removed from office immediately upon the second house passing the resolution
No separate Presidential order or notification required — automatic constitutional effect
Vice President takes over as Acting President under Article 65
UPSC trap: Removal is immediate and self-executing — contrast with removal of judges which requires a Presidential order

concepts.name: Judicial Review of Impeachment Proceedings
key_dimensions: No explicit constitutional bar on judicial review of impeachment
Debate: Whether impeachment is a 'political question' immune from judicial scrutiny
Sub-Committee of Congress Party v. Union of India — courts have generally been reluctant to intervene in parliamentary proceedings
Article 122 (courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament) as a potential shield against judicial review of impeachment

concepts.name: Impeachment vs. Removal Due to Incapacity or Death
key_dimensions: Article 61 covers only 'violation of Constitution' — not incapacity or death
No constitutional provision for removal of President on grounds of physical/mental incapacity (a noted gap)
Comparison with US 25th Amendment which provides for incapacity removal — India has no equivalent
UPSC trap: Students assume impeachment covers all removal scenarios — it covers ONLY constitutional violation

concepts.name: Impeachment During Prorogued or Dissolved Parliament
key_dimensions: Impeachment requires an active session — a prorogued Parliament cannot conduct impeachment
President can be summoned for a special session, but President also has role in summoning Parliament (Article 85) — constitutional tension
If Lok Sabha is dissolved and Rajya Sabha initiates, practical completion of process becomes impossible
Theoretical gap: Constitution does not explicitly resolve this scenario — deliberate or oversight ambiguity
